text: quick run-down on some of the advancements...... specialty sunglasses: these are good for blocking harmful UV rays and takes care of your facial health besides allowing you to see more clearly when the sun is on full blast. vests: another practical yet popular accesory, used to be everywhere at trail hikes in the past but now has spilled over to the road racing crowd. Useful for carrying stuff along with you during the race - extra water bottles (water and gatorade still available at almost all races though - it's a must), keys, bananas (or gels for nutrition)...... light attachments: more of a safety measure that allows you to be more visible at night or in low light conditions. running clothing: gone were the days where you'd just pick a random shirt and run - modern running clothing is meant to soak up sweat like a sponge, dry quickly, and be light enough to not bog you down while running. running shoes: running shoes nowadays are diverse - super-bouncy, carbon plated racing shoes loaded with advanced materials for the record breakers; super-cushioned, ultra-comfy running shoes for those who want to feel like running in Jello; old-school lightweight racing flats enhanced with the newest cushioning tech for the old-timers, et cetera...... watches and tracking: nowadays instead of flexing oyster perpetuals that cost more than a Toyota Corolla, you flex stats like your VO2Max, running pace, race readiness, et cetera, all being kept track of by the latest running smartwatches. text: There has been an explosion on hobbyist gear and consumer spending in general in the last 20 or so years. A small chunk of it is legit gear improvements and new tech. Stuff like basic HR monitors and shoe tech really is better than pedometers and 90s shoes. A big chunk of it is branding & "Keeping up with the Jones's". People used to flex with jewelry but smart gadgets are for sure this generation's "thing" to show off. Ditto for brand name apparel and gear. You don't need "high performance water bottles" to run at an amateur level and everyone who buys them knows that deep down. A HUGE chunk in every sport/hobby right now is "buy X and you'll magically get better". This has obviously always been around but influencers and mainstream pseudoscience have made it much more prevalent. I remember those fake 'magnet bracelets' that claimed to improve your balance like 20 years ago - it was a real turning point in how I see the general public interacting with "gear". Like 30% of people refuse to think for themselves and will buy and believe whatever you put in front of them. I see this from running to video games to golf to chess to weightlifting. Stuff that would've gotten you laughed at IRL is taken super duper Cereal now.
